headline: Record revenue, raised guidance; deal costs cut GAAP profit
summary_short: Q2 revenue rose 21% y/y to a record $1,947M and adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations climbed 13% to $638M, but GAAP earnings from operations fell 10% y/y to $372M on acquisition and portfolio-rationalization charges.
summary_long: Record Q2 revenue (+21% y/y) and adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations (+13%) reflected a full quarter of Quikrete contributions, a partial quarter of New Frontier Materials, and 2.3% organic aggregates shipment growth on infrastructure and nonresidential demand. GAAP operating income and diluted EPS fell y/y on $58M of acquisition, divestiture, integration and inventory step-up charges plus a portfolio-rationalization charge; adjusted diluted EPS still rose 3% to $5.00. Six-month operating cash flow dropped to $339M from $605M on higher tax payments tied to February's Midlothian/Texas ready-mix divestiture gain. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $7.2B-$7.4B and reaffirmed Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.36B-$2.5B, excluding any contribution from the pending $13.5B Lhoist North America acquisition announced June 27.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites record Q2 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations, driven by organic performance plus Quikrete and New Frontier Materials contributions, with infrastructure and heavy nonresidential demand supporting shipments.

Aggregates shipments +17% on a full quarter of Quikrete contributions, a partial quarter of NFM, and 2.3% organic growth from infrastructure/nonresidential demand; Specialties and Other Building Materials revenue also grew.

Aggregates gross profit -3% on a $52M non-cash inventory step-up charge from acquisition accounting; Other Building Materials margin fell on higher ready-mix raw material costs and weaker paving jobs; Specialties gross profit hit a record.

Earnings from operations fell as acquisition/divestiture/integration expenses and the inventory step-up charge (combined $58M) plus an asset and portfolio rationalization charge weighed on the quarter, per the release's own reconciliation notes.
Includes a $5M loss from discontinued operations this quarter versus a $36M gain a year ago; continuing-operations net earnings fell 12% on the acquisition-related charges noted above.

Includes $0.74/share of acquisition, divestiture, integration and inventory step-up charges plus a rationalization charge; continuing-operations diluted EPS was $4.26 before those items, and adjusted diluted EPS rose 3% to $5.00.

Six-month operating cash flow fell to $339M from $605M, primarily on higher income tax payments tied to the taxable gain from February's Midlothian/Texas ready-mix divestiture, plus $733M of net acquisition spending in the period.

H1 2026 cash flow shows $1,085M of new borrowings against $460M of repayments; the release separately discloses a July 15 commitment for a $1.5B term loan tied to the pending LNA transaction, not yet drawn at quarter-end.
